newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Smith&Nephew profit steady, keen to buy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Smith&Nephew profit steady, keen to buy.

text.p: Healthcare group Smith & Nephew Plc on Tuesday reported a one percent rise in 1996 profits and dismissed revived takeover talk as lacking all foundation.

The company, whose products range from sticking plasters to artificial knees, said there was no need to merge, adding it was looking for acquisitions instead to boost its leading presence in a consolidating industry.
Pre-tax profit before exceptional items rose to 182.2 million pounds ($295.7 million) from 180.4 million as tough market conditions, especially in the United States, persisted.

The company maintained its share in all principal product and geographical markets. Currency strength had a modest impact on the results but will make itself felt more this year if the dollar and pound stay at current levels, Smith & Nephew said.
"In the really quite difficult market conditions that we were in last year, these are good results relative to the way our competitors have been performing," said chief executive John Robinson.
He will become chairman in June when Eric Kinder retires. Deputy chief executive Chris O'Donnell will in turn replace Robinson.
Smith & Nephew's results were at the lower end of market expectations and the firm's shares fell four pence to 187 pence in mid-morning trade.
They were boosted late last month as takeover rumours flared up, much to the surprise of Robinson.
"I found it amazing. Sitting where we sit, there is no basis at all for it," he told journalists.
Robinson said Smith & Nephew, which in October bought its South Korean distributors for around four million pounds, "will continue to look very actively for acquisitions."

Germany, where Smith & Nephew's presence is not very strong, would be an obvious choice for purchases. But the problem there is that there are far fewer buying opportunities than in the dynamic U.S. market, Robinson added.
Smith & Nephew expects to see consolidation in the orthopaedic sector and Robinson said, "We could well participate in that over the next year or two."
With gearing of just eight percent, Smith & Nephew can spend well over 500 million pounds without using equity, he added.

Speaking of the tough U.S. market, Robinson said conditions would improve only marginally after a spate of mergers among hospitals and the formation of healthcare buying groups depressed selling prices.
"It (the pressure) is likely to last, although probably not as severe as last year through this year," Robinson said.
The U.S. market makes up about 40 percent of group profits.
Smith & Nephew made strong progress in the fast growing Asian market but at the moment that region generates just over five percent of total profits.
It said it planned to launch its human tissue skin replacement product Dermagraft in Britain and the U.S. market in the second half of the year.
"The big event this year will be Dermagraft," said Robinson. "So, as we go forward, we are in pretty good shape."
Dermagraft will be sold in a market with an estimated size of 1.5 billion pounds and Robinson, citing "observers", said the product should be able to grab a 10 to 12.5 percent market share.
